clue_checks.clue: I left Ur of the Chaldees.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 15:7 has the LORD saying He brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees. Lot also left Ur (Genesis 11:31), but an early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: God changed my name.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 17:5 records God changing Abram's name to Abraham. Jacob's name was also changed (Genesis 32:28), but later clues rule him out.

clue_checks.clue: My wife laughed at God's promise of a son.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 18:12 says Sarah laughed within herself. The surrounding context (18:10) makes clear she was laughing at the promise of a son, so this is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: God tested me in the land of Moriah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 22:1-2 says God did tempt (test) Abraham and sent him to the land of Moriah.

clue_checks.clue: I was a tiller of the ground.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:2 states Cain was a tiller of the ground.

clue_checks.clue: God did not respect my offering.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:5 says unto Cain and his offering he had not respect; 'the LORD' is implied from 4:4.

clue_checks.clue: I asked: Am I my brother's keeper?
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:9 records Cain's reply verbatim.

clue_checks.clue: God set a mark upon me.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 4:15 says the LORD set a mark upon Cain.

clue_checks.clue: I was formed of the dust of the ground.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:7 states the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground; in context this man is Adam.

clue_checks.clue: I gave names to the animals.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:20 explicitly says Adam gave names to all cattle, fowl, and beasts of the field.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in the garden of Eden.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 2:15 says the LORD God put the man into the garden of Eden; contextually this is Adam.

clue_checks.clue: My wife was Eve.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 3:20 says Adam called his wife's name Eve.

clue_checks.clue: I was the youngest son of Jesse.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:14 states David was the youngest. The surrounding verses (17:12-13) identify these as the sons of Jesse.

clue_checks.clue: I played the harp for King Saul.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:23 explicitly says David took a harp and played it, refreshing Saul.

clue_checks.clue: I defeated Goliath.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 17:50 says David prevailed over and slew 'the Philistine', whom the context (17:4, 17:23) names as Goliath.

clue_checks.clue: I became king over Israel.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 5:3 says they anointed David king over Israel. Saul and Solomon were also kings, but clues are revealed one at a time and the full set fits only David.

clue_checks.clue: I was a mighty man of wealth in Bethlehem.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 2:1 calls Boaz 'a mighty man of wealth' but does not mention Bethlehem. His link to Bethlehem appears in Ruth 2:4 ('Boaz came from Bethlehem').

clue_checks.clue: I let a Moabite woman glean in my fields.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 2:8 shows Boaz telling Ruth to glean in his field and stay there. It does not call her a Moabite; that is in Ruth 2:2 and 2:6 ('Ruth the Moabitess', 'the Moabitish damsel').

clue_checks.clue: I redeemed the inheritance of Elimelech.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 4:9 has Boaz declare he has 'bought all that was Elimelech's'. Calling this 'redeemed' fits the kinsman-redeemer context and is acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I married Ruth.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 4:13 says 'Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife'.

clue_checks.clue: My name is interpreted 'the son of consolation'.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 4:36 states Joses was surnamed Barnabas, 'being interpreted, The son of consolation.'

clue_checks.clue: I sold land and laid the money at the apostles' feet.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 4:37 says he sold land and laid the money at the apostles' feet.

clue_checks.clue: I brought Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 9:27 says Barnabas brought Saul to the apostles. 'Jerusalem' is not in the quoted verse but comes from the context in Acts 9:26. This is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I travelled with Paul on his first missionary journey.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 13:2-4 shows Barnabas and Saul sent out together to Seleucia and Cyprus. 'First missionary journey' is a conventional label. Mark also went along (Acts 13:5), but the earlier clues uniquely identify Barnabas.

clue_checks.clue: I was taken captive to Babylon as a young man.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 1:3-6 calls Daniel one of the 'children' of Israel brought to stand in the king's palace and taught the Chaldean tongue, which supports 'young.' The quoted text does not explicitly say 'captive' or 'Babylon'; that context comes from Daniel 1:1-2. The clue is reasonable but goes slightly beyond the cited verses. It also fits Ezekiel as an early clue, which is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I purposed not to defile myself with the king's meat.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 1:8 states that Daniel purposed in his heart not to defile himself with the portion of the king's meat.

clue_checks.clue: I read the writing on the wall.
clue_checks.reason: In Daniel 5:17 Daniel says, 'I will read the writing unto the king.' The wall is identified in Daniel 5:5, and this paraphrase is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I was delivered from the den of lions.
clue_checks.reason: Daniel 6:22-23 records God shutting the lions' mouths and Daniel being taken up out of the den unhurt.

clue_checks.clue: I walked with God.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:22 states Enoch walked with God. Noah also walked with God (Genesis 6:9), but this is an early clue and later clues exclude him.

clue_checks.clue: I was the father of Methuselah.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:21 states Enoch begat Methuselah.

clue_checks.clue: I was not, for God took me.
clue_checks.reason: This matches Genesis 5:24 directly.

clue_checks.clue: Hebrews says I was translated so I should not see death.
clue_checks.reason: Hebrews 11:5 states Enoch was translated that he should not see death.

clue_checks.clue: I was ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen when I was called.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 19:19 says Elisha was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen when Elijah cast his mantle upon him, which was his call.

clue_checks.clue: I asked for a double portion of my master's spirit.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:9 records Elisha asking Elijah for a double portion of his spirit.

clue_checks.clue: I took up the mantle that fell from Elijah.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:13 says 'He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him'. In context (v.12), 'he' is Elisha.

clue_checks.clue: I told Naaman to wash in the Jordan seven times.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:10 says Elisha sent this instruction to Naaman by a messenger. 'Told' is an acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Tishbite.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:1 explicitly calls him 'Elijah the Tishbite.'

clue_checks.clue: Ravens fed me by the brook Cherith.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 17:6 says the ravens brought him bread and flesh and that he drank of the brook, but it does not name Cherith or Elijah. Those details come from vv. 3-5, which the item's reference_label (17:1-6) does cover.

clue_checks.clue: I challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 18:19-24 records Elijah gathering the prophets of Baal to Mount Carmel and proposing the test of the God that answers by fire.

clue_checks.clue: I went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 2:11 states 'Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.'

clue_checks.clue: I was one of the twelve spies.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 13:6 names Caleb son of Jephunneh as Judah's representative among the men sent to spy out Canaan, one from each of the twelve tribes.

clue_checks.clue: I brought back a good report with Joshua.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 14:6-9 shows Joshua and Caleb together calling the land 'exceeding good' and urging the people not to fear.

clue_checks.clue: I was eighty-five years old when I asked for my inheritance.
clue_checks.reason: In Joshua 14:10 Caleb, the speaker from v.6, says 'I am this day fourscore and five years old' as he requests his inheritance.

clue_checks.clue: I asked for the mountain and received Hebron.
clue_checks.reason: In Joshua 14:12-13 Caleb says 'give me this mountain', and Joshua gives Caleb Hebron for an inheritance.

suggested_fix: The clues, answer and explanation are accurate, and together the clues fit only Caleb. The hint 'Look in Joshua.' is ambiguous, though, because 'Joshua' is also one of the options and could be read as pointing to that person. Reword it to clearly mean the book, e.g. 'Look in the book of Joshua, chapter 14.' or 'This man spoke to Joshua at Gilgal.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophetess.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:4 calls Deborah 'a prophetess.' Miriam and Huldah were also prophetesses, but this is an early clue and the later clues narrow the answer.

clue_checks.clue: I judged Israel under a palm tree in mount Ephraim.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:4-5 says she judged Israel and dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah in mount Ephraim, where Israel came to her for judgment. The clue is an acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I summoned Barak to fight Sisera.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 4:6-7 says she sent for and called Barak and relayed the LORD's command to fight Sisera's forces at the river Kishon.

clue_checks.clue: A song of mine is recorded in Judges 5.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 5:1 says 'Then sang Deborah and Barak.' The song is attributed to her together with Barak, so the clue's wording is fair.

clue_checks.clue: I was a cunning hunter.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:27 says Esau was a cunning hunter. Nimrod is called a mighty hunter, but an early clue fitting another option is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I was born red and hairy.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:25 says the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and he was named Esau.

clue_checks.clue: I sold my birthright for a meal.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:33-34 says he sold his birthright unto Jacob and was then given bread and pottage of lentiles.

clue_checks.clue: I am also called Edom.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 36:1 says 'Esau, who is Edom.'

clue_checks.clue: An angel found me threshing wheat by a winepress.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 6:11-12 says Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress when the angel of the LORD appeared to him.

clue_checks.clue: I tested God with a fleece.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 6:36-40 describes Gideon's two fleece tests ('let me prove... with the fleece').

clue_checks.clue: My army was reduced to three hundred men.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 7:7 has the LORD saving Israel by the three hundred men who lapped and sending the rest home. Together with 7:2-6, this is a reduction to 300.

clue_checks.clue: We carried trumpets, pitchers and lamps.
clue_checks.reason: Judges 7:16 says each of the three hundred received a trumpet and an empty pitcher with a lamp inside.

clue_checks.clue: I saw the Lord high and lifted up in the year King Uzziah died.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 6:1 states that in the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord on a throne, high and lifted up.

clue_checks.clue: A seraph touched my lips with a live coal.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 6:6-7 says one of the seraphims laid a live coal upon his mouth and said, 'this hath touched thy lips.'

clue_checks.clue: I answered: Here am I; send me.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 6:8 quotes this response exactly.

clue_checks.clue: I prophesied of a child called Immanuel.
clue_checks.reason: Isaiah 7:14 foretells a son whose name shall be called Immanuel. The context (7:3, 7:10-13) shows the word comes through Isaiah to Ahaz.

clue_checks.clue: I was born holding my twin brother's heel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:26 says the second twin's hand took hold on Esau's heel and he was named Jacob.

clue_checks.clue: I bought my brother's birthright with pottage.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 25:33-34 says Esau sold his birthright to Jacob, and Jacob gave him bread and pottage of lentiles.

clue_checks.clue: I dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 28:12 describes the dream of a ladder whose top reached to heaven. The context (28:10) identifies the dreamer as Jacob.

clue_checks.clue: God renamed me Israel.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 32:28 gives the renaming from Jacob to Israel. In the wider context, the one who wrestled with Jacob is linked with God (32:30), and Genesis 35:10 explicitly has God rename him. The clue is fully accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I was raised by my cousin Mordecai.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:7 says Mordecai brought up Esther, 'his uncle's daughter' (his cousin), and took her for his own daughter after her parents died.

clue_checks.clue: I became queen in Persia.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 2:17 says the king made her queen instead of Vashti. Persia is not named in this verse, but the king is Ahasuerus of Persia (Esther 1:3), so this is a fair paraphrase. Vashti also fits this clue alone, which is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I said: If I perish, I perish.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 4:16 records Esther's words verbatim: 'and if I perish, I perish.'

clue_checks.clue: The feast of Purim remembers my people's deliverance.
clue_checks.reason: Esther 9:26-28 establishes Purim as a yearly memorial kept by the Jews. Esther's Jewish identity is established in the book (Esther 2:10), so 'my people' applies to her.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in the land of Uz.
clue_checks.reason: Job 1:1 places Job in the land of Uz. The friends are identified as Temanite, Shuhite, and Buzite.

clue_checks.clue: I was perfect and upright.
clue_checks.reason: Job 1:1 says 'that man was perfect and upright.'

clue_checks.clue: I lost my children and possessions in a single day.
clue_checks.reason: Job 1:13 says 'there was a day', and the messengers arrive one after another ('While he was yet speaking'). They report the loss of oxen, asses, sheep, camels, servants, and his sons and daughters.

clue_checks.clue: I said: The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away.
clue_checks.reason: This is a direct quotation of Job 1:21.

clue_checks.clue: God said He knew me before He formed me in the belly.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 1:5 says, "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee," spoken by God to Jeremiah.

clue_checks.clue: I protested that I was only a child.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 1:6 says, "Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child." The word "only" is acceptable paraphrase of the protest.

clue_checks.clue: I was let down into a dungeon full of mire.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 38:6 says they "let down Jeremiah with cords" into a dungeon where "there was no water, but mire," and he "sunk in the mire." "Full of mire" is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: Baruch wrote my words on a roll.
clue_checks.reason: Jeremiah 36:4 says Baruch "wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD... upon a roll of a book." "My words" is a reasonable paraphrase, since Baruch wrote what Jeremiah dictated.

clue_checks.clue: My husband was Elkanah.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:2 names Hannah as one of 'his' two wives, but Elkanah is named only in 1:1, so the quoted text does not show the husband's name. The clue also fits Peninnah, which is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I prayed silently at Shiloh, and Eli thought I was drunk.
clue_checks.reason: 1:13 supports the silent prayer and Eli thinking she was drunken. The Shiloh location comes from 1:9, not the quoted verse.

clue_checks.clue: I vowed to give my son to the LORD.
clue_checks.reason: 1:11: she vowed that if given a man child, 'I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life.'

clue_checks.clue: I named my son Samuel.
clue_checks.reason: 1:20: she 'bare a son, and called his name Samuel.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a prophet, the son of Amittai.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 14:25 calls him 'Jonah, the son of Amittai, the prophet.'

clue_checks.clue: I fled from God's call on a ship.
clue_checks.reason: Jonah 1:3 says Jonah fled from the presence of the LORD on a ship going to Tarshish.

clue_checks.clue: I spent three days inside a great fish.
clue_checks.reason: Jonah 1:17 says Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

clue_checks.clue: I was displeased when Nineveh repented.
clue_checks.reason: Jonah 4:1 says it displeased Jonah exceedingly. The verse itself does not name Nineveh's repentance. In context (3:10), what displeased him was God sparing the city after it repented. This is acceptable paraphrase but slightly compressed.

clue_checks.clue: My father Zacharias was a priest.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 1:5 establishes that Zacharias was a priest and that his wife was Elisabeth. It does not say he was John's father. That comes later, in Luke 1:13 and 1:57-63.

clue_checks.clue: I wore raiment of camel's hair.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 3:4 states that John had his raiment of camel's hair.

clue_checks.clue: I ate locusts and wild honey.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 3:4 states that John's meat was locusts and wild honey.

clue_checks.clue: I baptized Jesus in the Jordan.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 1:9 states that Jesus was baptized of John in Jordan.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of the twelve.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:14 calls Judas Iscariot 'one of the twelve.' This early clue also fits the other options, which is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: I had the bag.
clue_checks.reason: John 12:6 says he 'had the bag.' The quoted verse does not name him, but John 12:4 identifies the speaker as Judas Iscariot.

clue_checks.clue: I agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:15: 'I will deliver him unto you... they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.'

clue_checks.clue: I betrayed Jesus with a kiss.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:48-49 says 'he that betrayed him' gave the sign of a kiss and 'kissed him.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a son of Zebedee.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:21 names 'James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother' with 'Zebedee their father.' It also fits James, but as an early clue that is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus surnamed my brother and me Boanerges.
clue_checks.reason: Mark 3:17 says Jesus surnamed James and John 'Boanerges.' It also fits James, but later clues exclude him.

clue_checks.clue: Tradition identifies me as the disciple whom Jesus loved.
clue_checks.reason: John 13:23 mentions the disciple 'whom Jesus loved' but does not name him. The clue is honestly framed as tradition, so it is acceptable, though not strictly textual.

clue_checks.clue: I was on the isle of Patmos for the word of God.
clue_checks.reason: Revelation 1:9 says 'I John... was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God,' which matches the answer 'John.' Equating this John with the apostle is traditional, and the explanation acknowledges that.

clue_checks.clue: I was my father's favourite son.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 37:3 says Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, which matches 'favourite son.'

clue_checks.clue: My brothers sold me into slavery.
clue_checks.reason: In Genesis 37:28 the subject of 'they drew... and sold Joseph' is grammatically ambiguous and could be read as the Midianites. The verse also does not use the word slavery. Genesis 45:4 ('whom ye sold into Egypt') states the brothers' role more clearly. The clue is consistent with the narrative but not cleanly proven by this verse alone.

clue_checks.clue: I interpreted Pharaoh's dreams.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 41:25 shows Joseph explaining to Pharaoh what his dream means.

clue_checks.clue: I was set over all the land of Egypt.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 41:41 matches the clue directly.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of twelve men sent to spy out Canaan.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 13:8 lists Oshea the son of Nun of Ephraim among the spies. The quoted verse does not mention the number twelve or identify Oshea as Joshua. Numbers 13:16 states that Moses called Oshea 'Jehoshua'. The clue also fits Caleb, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I succeeded Moses as leader.
clue_checks.reason: After Moses' death, the LORD commissions Joshua the son of Nun to lead all the people over Jordan, which clearly depicts succession.

clue_checks.clue: The walls of Jericho fell when the people shouted.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 6:20 confirms the walls fell flat at the people's shout. The verse does not mention Joshua, and the clue is not phrased about the answer. Joshua's leadership at Jericho is shown in Joshua 6:2-16.

clue_checks.clue: I said: As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.
clue_checks.reason: The quote matches Joshua 24:15 exactly. The speaker is not named in verse 15 itself; Joshua 24:2 establishes that Joshua is speaking.

clue_checks.clue: I was a seller of purple.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:14 explicitly calls Lydia 'a seller of purple.'

clue_checks.clue: I came from the city of Thyatira.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:14 says Lydia was 'of the city of Thyatira.'

clue_checks.clue: I heard Paul speak by a riverside at Philippi.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:13 describes speaking to women by a river side outside the city, but it names neither Philippi (named in 16:12) nor Lydia. Lydia's hearing comes from 16:14. The clue is accurate in context but adds detail beyond the cited verse.

clue_checks.clue: My household was baptized.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:15: 'when she was baptized, and her household.'

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Bethany with my sister and brother.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:1 names Bethany as the town of Mary and her sister Martha and says Lazarus was of Bethany. It does not call Lazarus their brother; that comes in John 11:2. Neither verse says they lived together in one household.

clue_checks.clue: I was cumbered about much serving.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:40 says this of Martha almost word for word.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said my sister had chosen the good part.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:42 says Mary chose that good part, and Luke 10:39 identifies Mary as Martha's sister. The verse is the second half of Jesus' reply to Martha, so 'Jesus said' is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I welcomed Jesus into my house.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 10:38 says Martha received him into her house.

clue_checks.clue: Seven devils had gone out of me.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 8:2 names Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils.

clue_checks.clue: I stood by the cross.
clue_checks.reason: John 19:25 lists Mary Magdalene standing by the cross. Mary the mother of James and Salome are also placed at the crucifixion (Mark 15:40), but this early clue need not be unique.

clue_checks.clue: I came to the tomb while it was yet dark.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:1 says Mary Magdalene came early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre.

clue_checks.clue: At first I supposed the risen Jesus was the gardener.
clue_checks.reason: In John 20:15 she supposes him to be the gardener, and John 20:16 confirms the speaker is Mary. This clue fits only Mary Magdalene among the options.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Nazareth of Galilee.
clue_checks.reason: Gabriel was sent to Nazareth, a city of Galilee, to the virgin named Mary. This places her there, and Luke 2:4 also links Joseph and Mary to Nazareth.

clue_checks.clue: The angel Gabriel was sent to me.
clue_checks.reason: The text says Gabriel was sent from God to a virgin whose name was Mary.

clue_checks.clue: I was espoused to Joseph.
clue_checks.reason: The text names Mary as a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph.

clue_checks.clue: I gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 2:4-7 shows Mary bringing forth her firstborn son in Bethlehem, but the name Jesus does not appear in these verses. It is given in Luke 2:21. The identification is clear from context, so this is a minor overreach.

clue_checks.clue: My father was Enoch.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:21 states Enoch begat Methuselah.

clue_checks.clue: My son was Lamech.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:25 states Methuselah begat Lamech.

clue_checks.clue: I was Noah's grandfather.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:28-29 shows Lamech begat Noah but does not name Methuselah. The grandfather relationship holds only together with Genesis 5:25. Taken with that verse, it is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I lived nine hundred sixty and nine years.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 5:27 states that all the days of Methuselah were 969 years.

clue_checks.clue: I lived in Bethany.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:1 names 'Lazarus, of Bethany.' Simon the leper was also in Bethany, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: My sisters were Mary and Martha.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:2 says Mary's 'brother Lazarus was sick,' and 11:1 calls Martha Mary's sister. So both are his sisters.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus wept near my grave.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:35 says only 'Jesus wept.' The setting near Lazarus's grave comes from context in 11:34 ('Where have ye laid him?... Come and see'), not from the cited verse. The citing could be widened to John 11:34-35.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called me out of the tomb.
clue_checks.reason: John 11:43-44: 'Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth.'

clue_checks.clue: I was king of Salem.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 14:18 explicitly calls Melchizedek 'king of Salem.'

clue_checks.clue: I was priest of the most high God.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 14:18 states 'he was the priest of the most high God.'

clue_checks.clue: I brought forth bread and wine to Abram.
clue_checks.reason: Verse 18 says Melchizedek 'brought forth bread and wine' but does not name a recipient. Abram is clearly implied by context (vv. 17, 19), so this is a minor addition.

clue_checks.clue: Abram gave me tithes of all.
clue_checks.reason: Verse 20 says 'he gave him tithes of all' with ambiguous pronouns. Context, and Hebrews 7:4, show that Abram gave the tithes to Melchizedek, but the cited verse alone does not name either party.

clue_checks.clue: I watched over my baby brother at the river.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:4 says 'his sister stood afar off' to see what would happen, but it does not name her. The river setting comes from 2:3. Identifying her as Miriam relies on context such as Numbers 26:59, which names Miriam as Moses' sister. The clue is reasonable but not fully supported by the cited verse alone.

clue_checks.clue: I am called a prophetess.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 15:20 explicitly says 'Miriam the prophetess.' Deborah is also a prophetess, but this is an early clue and the full set excludes her.

clue_checks.clue: I led the women with a timbrel after the Red Sea crossing.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 15:20 says she took a timbrel and all the women went out after her. The Red Sea context comes from 15:19-21. This is acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was briefly struck with leprosy.
clue_checks.reason: Numbers 12:10 confirms she became leprous, but 'briefly' is not in this verse. It is implied by 12:14-15, where she is shut out for seven days.

clue_checks.clue: I was a publican.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 10:3 explicitly says 'Matthew the publican.'

clue_checks.clue: I sat at the receipt of custom.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 9:9 says Jesus saw Matthew 'sitting at the receipt of custom.'

clue_checks.clue: Jesus said to me: Follow me.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 9:9 records Jesus saying to Matthew, 'Follow me.'

clue_checks.clue: Jesus ate with publicans and sinners at my table.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 5:29-30 names Levi, not Matthew. Applying it to Matthew relies on the parallel accounts (Mark 2:14; Matthew 9:9-10) to equate the two. The text also says 'in his own house' rather than 'at my table.' Matthew 9:10 would be a more direct reference, though it only says 'the house.'

clue_checks.clue: I was cupbearer to King Artaxerxes.
clue_checks.reason: Nehemiah 1:11 says only 'I was the king's cupbearer' and does not name the king. Artaxerxes is named in Nehemiah 2:1, so the reference should be 1:11 with 2:1.

clue_checks.clue: I wept over Jerusalem's broken walls.
clue_checks.reason: Nehemiah 1:3-4 reports that the wall was broken down and that Nehemiah sat down and wept.

clue_checks.clue: I led the rebuilding of the city wall.
clue_checks.reason: In Nehemiah 2:17-18, Nehemiah calls the people to build the wall and they respond, 'Let us rise up and build.'

clue_checks.clue: The wall was finished in fifty-two days.
clue_checks.reason: Nehemiah 6:15 says the wall was finished 'in fifty and two days.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a fisherman, the brother of Andrew.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:18 names 'Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother' and says 'they were fishers.'

clue_checks.clue: Jesus called me to become a fisher of men.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 4:19 records Jesus saying to Peter and Andrew, 'I will make you fishers of men.' This clue also fits Andrew, but that is acceptable for a single clue.

clue_checks.clue: I walked on the water toward Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 14:29 explicitly says Peter came down out of the ship and 'walked on the water, to go to Jesus.'

clue_checks.clue: I denied Jesus three times before the cock crew.
clue_checks.reason: Matthew 26:75 gives Jesus' prediction and Peter's bitter weeping, which implies the denials took place. The three denials themselves are narrated in verses 69-74, so 26:69-75 would be a fuller reference.

clue_checks.clue: I was captain of the host of the king of Syria.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:1 calls Naaman 'captain of the host of the king of Syria.'

clue_checks.clue: I was a leper.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:1 ends 'but he was a leper.' Gehazi later became leprous (5:27), but early clues may fit other options.

clue_checks.clue: A captive little maid from Israel told of a prophet.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:2-3 says a captive little maid who waited on Naaman's wife spoke of the prophet in Samaria who could recover 'my lord' of his leprosy.

clue_checks.clue: I dipped myself seven times in the Jordan.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Kings 5:14 says he 'dipped himself seven times in Jordan.' It refers to Naaman.

clue_checks.clue: I lived before a great flood.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 7:6 says Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came, so he lived before it. The clue also fits Enoch, but it is an early clue, which is acceptable.

clue_checks.clue: God told me to build with gopher wood.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 6:14: 'Make thee an ark of gopher wood' is God's direct command to Noah (see v.13).

clue_checks.clue: My sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.
clue_checks.reason: Genesis 6:10 states Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

clue_checks.clue: I built the ark.
clue_checks.reason: Hebrews 11:7 says Noah 'prepared an ark to the saving of his house.'

clue_checks.clue: As a baby I was hidden in an ark of bulrushes.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:3 describes the child (Moses, per context in 2:1-10) being placed in an ark of bulrushes after he could no longer be hidden.

clue_checks.clue: I was raised in Pharaoh's household.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 2:10 says the child was brought to Pharaoh's daughter and became her son, so 'raised in Pharaoh's household' is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I saw a bush burn without being consumed.
clue_checks.reason: Exodus 3:2 says the bush burned with fire and was not consumed. Verses 3:1 and 3:4 identify the viewer as Moses.

clue_checks.clue: I led Israel out of Egypt.
clue_checks.reason: In Acts 7:35-36 Stephen says Moses brought them out after showing wonders in Egypt, the Red Sea, and the wilderness.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews.
clue_checks.reason: John 3:1 states Nicodemus was 'a man of the Pharisees' and 'a ruler of the Jews.'

clue_checks.clue: I came to Jesus by night.
clue_checks.reason: John 3:2 says 'The same came to Jesus by night,' referring to Nicodemus.

clue_checks.clue: Jesus told me I must be born again.
clue_checks.reason: In John 3:7 Jesus tells Nicodemus, 'Ye must be born again,' continuing the conversation that began in 3:3.

clue_checks.clue: I brought myrrh and aloes for Jesus' burial.
clue_checks.reason: John 19:39 says Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes. Joseph of Arimathaea asked for the body, but the text attributes the spices to Nicodemus.

clue_checks.clue: I was a Nazarite from birth.
clue_checks.reason: Samson says, 'I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb.' This matches 'from birth' as a minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I tore a young lion with my bare hands.
clue_checks.reason: The text says 'he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand.'

clue_checks.clue: Delilah learned the secret of my strength.
clue_checks.reason: Samson 'told her all his heart,' explaining that shaving would remove his strength, and Delilah recognized this.

clue_checks.clue: I pulled down the house where the Philistines gathered.
clue_checks.reason: Samson took hold of the pillars and bowed himself, and the house fell upon the lords and all the people therein.

clue_checks.clue: I was a woman of Moab.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:4 names Ruth among the 'women of Moab' taken as wives. It also fits Orpah, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: I told my mother-in-law: whither thou goest, I will go.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 1:16 records Ruth saying 'whither thou goest, I will go' to Naomi, her mother-in-law.

clue_checks.clue: I gleaned in the fields of Boaz.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 2:3 says she (Ruth, per 2:2) gleaned on 'a part of the field belonging unto Boaz.' The plural 'fields' is minor paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I became an ancestor of King David.
clue_checks.reason: Ruth 4:13-17 says Ruth bore Obed, 'the father of Jesse, the father of David,' making her David's great-grandmother.

clue_checks.clue: My house was upon the town wall of Jericho.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:15 says her house was upon the town wall. Jericho is not named in that verse, but Joshua 2:1-3 establishes the city, so the clue is a fair paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I hid two Israelite spies.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:4 says she took the two men and hid them. Joshua 2:1-2 identifies them as spies sent by Joshua, of the children of Israel.

clue_checks.clue: I let them down by a cord through a window.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:15 matches this nearly word for word.

clue_checks.clue: A line of scarlet thread marked my home.
clue_checks.reason: Joshua 2:18 is only the spies' instruction to bind the scarlet line in the window. Rahab actually binds it in 2:21, and its purpose as a marker comes from context. Still an acceptable paraphrase.

clue_checks.clue: I was born in Tarsus.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 22:3 has Paul saying he was 'born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia.'

clue_checks.clue: I once persecuted the church.
clue_checks.reason: Galatians 1:13 says 'beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it.'

clue_checks.clue: A light from heaven blinded me near Damascus.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 22:6-11 describes a great light from heaven 'nigh unto Damascus' and says 'I could not see for the glory of that light.'

clue_checks.clue: I wrote many letters to the churches.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Peter 3:15-16 refers to 'all his epistles,' which implies several letters. It does not say 'many' or that they were addressed 'to the churches.' This is a reasonable paraphrase but adds detail not in the passage.

clue_checks.clue: I was of the tribe of Benjamin.
clue_checks.reason: In 1 Samuel 9:21 Saul calls himself 'a Benjamite.' Jonathan was also a Benjamite, but that is acceptable for an early clue.

clue_checks.clue: From my shoulders upward I was higher than any of the people.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 9:2 says this of Saul almost word for word.

clue_checks.clue: Samuel anointed me as Israel's first king.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 10:1 shows Samuel anointing Saul as 'captain over his inheritance.' The verse itself does not say 'first king.' The kingship is clear from the surrounding chapters (10:24, 11:15), and the claim is accurate.

clue_checks.clue: I consulted a woman at Endor.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 28:7-8 shows Saul seeking out and consulting the woman with a familiar spirit at Endor.

clue_checks.clue: I was chief among the publicans.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:2 states Zacchaeus was the chief among the publicans.

clue_checks.clue: I was rich.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:2 states 'and he was rich.'

clue_checks.clue: I was little of stature.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:3 states 'because he was little of stature.'

clue_checks.clue: I climbed a sycomore tree to see Jesus.
clue_checks.reason: Luke 19:4 states he climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of seven chosen to serve the church.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 6:3-5 names Stephen first among the seven chosen. Philip, another option, was also one of the seven, but this is acceptable for an early clue because the later clues narrow the answer to Stephen.

clue_checks.clue: I was full of faith and power.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 6:8 says this of Stephen in nearly the same words.

clue_checks.clue: As I spoke I saw the heavens opened.
clue_checks.reason: In Acts 7:56 Stephen says, "Behold, I see the heavens opened," during his speech.

clue_checks.clue: I was stoned while a young man named Saul watched.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 7:58 records the stoning and the witnesses laying their clothes at Saul's feet, and verse 59 names Stephen. That Saul was present and watching is a fair reading, also confirmed by Acts 8:1 and 22:20.

clue_checks.clue: My mother was Bathsheba.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Samuel 12:24 says Bath-sheba bore a son and David called his name Solomon.

clue_checks.clue: I asked God for an understanding heart.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 3:9 records the request for 'an understanding heart.' The surrounding context (3:5, 3:10) identifies the speaker as Solomon.

clue_checks.clue: I built the temple in Jerusalem.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Kings 6:14 says 'So Solomon built the house, and finished it.' Context (6:1) shows this is the house of the LORD.

clue_checks.clue: I judged between two women who both claimed one baby.
clue_checks.reason: The 1 Kings 3:16-28 passage supports the clue, but the supplied text stops at verse 23. It shows the dispute but not the king's judgment (vv. 24-27), and it does not name Solomon. The full cited range does support the clue.

clue_checks.clue: My mother Hannah prayed for me at Shiloh.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 1:10-11 records her prayer and vow for a man child. These verses do not name Hannah, mention Shiloh, or name Samuel. The Shiloh setting is in 1:9 and the naming of Samuel is in 1:20.

clue_checks.clue: As a boy I served Eli the priest.
clue_checks.reason: The text says the child Samuel 'ministered unto the LORD before Eli.' That is service to the LORD under Eli, not service to Eli himself, and this verse does not call Eli 'the priest' (1 Samuel 2:11 does).

clue_checks.clue: I heard the LORD call my name in the night.
clue_checks.reason: Verse 10 shows the LORD calling 'Samuel, Samuel.' The night setting comes from the context in 3:3, where Samuel was lying down before the lamp went out, not from this verse.

clue_checks.clue: I anointed both Saul and David.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Samuel 16:13 shows Samuel anointing David only. His anointing of Saul is in 1 Samuel 10:1, which is not cited.

clue_checks.clue: I was one of the twelve, called Didymus.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:24 explicitly calls Thomas 'one of the twelve, called Didymus.'

clue_checks.clue: I was absent when Jesus first appeared to the disciples.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:24 says Thomas 'was not with them when Jesus came,' which refers to the appearance to the gathered disciples in John 20:19. The word 'first' is not in the verse but is a fair reading of the context, since 20:26 records a later appearance. Luke 24:34-36 records earlier appearances to Simon and the Emmaus disciples, so 'first' is a slight overstatement.

clue_checks.clue: I wanted to see the print of the nails.
clue_checks.reason: In John 20:25 Thomas says, 'Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails... I will not believe.'

clue_checks.clue: I said: My Lord and my God.
clue_checks.reason: John 20:28: 'And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.'

clue_checks.clue: My grandmother Lois and mother Eunice shared unfeigned faith.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Timothy 1:5 says the unfeigned faith dwelt first in Lois and Eunice, and also in Timothy.

clue_checks.clue: I was Paul's young companion.
clue_checks.reason: Acts 16:1-3 shows Paul taking Timothy with him as a companion but says nothing about his youth. Youth is mentioned in 1 Timothy 4:12, which is not cited.

clue_checks.clue: Paul called me his dearly beloved son.
clue_checks.reason: 2 Timothy 1:2 reads 'To Timothy, my dearly beloved son.'

clue_checks.clue: Two New Testament letters are addressed to me.
clue_checks.reason: 1 Timothy 1:2 alone shows only one letter addressed to Timothy. Two letters is established only together with 2 Timothy 1:2.
